sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Fitness has come to be associated with special places and special clothing: the gymnasium with its machines, the running track, the class that meets at six in the morning. These have their uses, but they can obscure a simpler truth. For most of human history people were active not because they exercised but because their lives required it. They walked to fields and markets, carried water, ground grain and climbed hills. Physical activity was woven into the day rather than added to it as a separate task.

Many people today spend their waking hours seated, at a desk, in a vehicle or before a screen, and then try to compensate with an hour of vigorous effort. The hour is worth having, but it may not undo the effects of the remaining sedentary day. A growing body of opinion holds that the small movements of daily life matter more than was once assumed: climbing stairs instead of taking the lift, walking to the shop, standing up every half hour, doing household chores by hand. Such activity is unglamorous and earns no medals, but it has the advantage of being sustainable, since it demands no fees, no equipment and no special motivation. The aim, perhaps, is not to become an athlete but to recover a little of the ordinary movement that modern convenience has quietly taken away.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: In controlled trials, patients who receive an inert tablet in place of a real drug frequently report genuine improvement. This placebo response was long treated by researchers as a nuisance, a source of noise to be subtracted before the true effect of a medicine could be measured. More recent work has made it an object of study in its own right. It appears that expectation, attention and the ritual of treatment can measurably alter the experience of pain, nausea and fatigue, though they rarely shrink a tumour or clear an infection. The effect is strongest for symptoms that the brain itself helps to construct, and it is shaped by details as small as the colour of a pill or the warmth of a doctor's manner.

These findings carry an uncomfortable implication for practitioners of every system of medicine. A consultation that is hurried, impersonal or dismissive may make an effective drug less effective, while time spent listening carefully to a patient is not a courtesy but part of the treatment. At the same time, the placebo response cannot justify offering a remedy whose specific benefit has never been shown, for deception corrodes the trust on which the response itself depends. The honest lesson is that how a doctor treats a patient matters, in addition to, and never instead of, what the doctor prescribes.

questions.q: Which title best suits the passage?
opts: Why Exercise Is a Waste of Time
questions.why: Main idea: ordinary daily movement, once 'woven into the day', deserves to be recovered.

questions.q: According to the passage, for most of human history people were active because:
opts: They were advised to by physicians.
questions.why: Detail: 'people were active not because they exercised but because their lives required it'.

questions.q: The author suggests that an hour of vigorous exercise after a seated day:
opts: Fully cancels the effects of sitting.
Is useless and should be avoided.
Is more sustainable than daily movement.
Is worth having but may not be enough by itself.
questions.why: Inference: 'The hour is worth having, but it may not undo the effects of the remaining sedentary day'.

questions.q: The phrase "modern convenience has quietly taken away" suggests that:
opts: Convenience has made people more active.
The loss of everyday movement happened gradually and largely unnoticed.
People deliberately chose to stop moving.
questions.why: Inference/tone: 'quietly' implies the change crept in without people noticing.

questions.q: The word "sedentary" most nearly means:
questions.why: Vocabulary: people 'spend their waking hours seated, at a desk, in a vehicle or before a screen'.

questions.q: The main point of the passage is that:
opts: the placebo response shows that the doctor-patient relationship affects outcomes, but it must supplement, not replace, effective treatment.
placebos are as effective as real drugs for all illnesses.
researchers should ignore the placebo response as mere noise.
the colour of a pill is the most important factor in treatment.
questions.why: Main idea: 'how a doctor treats a patient matters, in addition to, and never instead of, what the doctor prescribes'.

questions.q: According to the passage, the placebo effect is strongest for:
opts: symptoms the brain itself helps to construct, such as pain and nausea.
questions.why: Detail: 'The effect is strongest for symptoms that the brain itself helps to construct'; it 'rarely' shrinks tumours or clears infections.

questions.q: The author would most likely disapprove of a practitioner who:
opts: prescribes an unproven remedy on the ground that the patient may feel better anyway.
studies the placebo response in controlled trials.
spends extra time listening to a patient's complaints.
explains a medicine's purpose warmly and clearly.
questions.why: Inference: 'the placebo response cannot justify offering a remedy whose specific benefit has never been shown'.

questions.q: In referring to 'practitioners of every system of medicine', the author intends to:
opts: claim that all drugs are no better than placebos.
attack one particular system of medicine.
indicate that the lesson applies to all practitioners, not to any one tradition.
argue that consultations should be made shorter.
questions.why: Purpose: the implication is 'uncomfortable' for everyone, since any 'hurried, impersonal or dismissive' consultation can weaken an effective drug.

questions.q: As used in the passage, 'inert' means:
questions.why: Vocabulary: an 'inert tablet' is given 'in place of a real drug', i.e. it contains no active ingredient.

questions.q: In the sentence “The book that you lent me is interesting,” the clause “that you lent me” is a:
questions.why: It qualifies the noun 'book', so it is an adjective clause. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “Despite of the heavy rain, the match continued.”
questions.why: 'Despite' is never followed by 'of'; 'in spite of' or 'despite'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The lawyer gave the family sound ____ on the matter.”
questions.why: 'Counsel' means advice; 'council' means an administrative body. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “He needs not go there today.”
questions.why: As a modal, 'need' takes no -s: 'He need not go' (or 'does not need to go'). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “sporadic”:
questions.why: 'Sporadic' means occurring at irregular intervals; 'constant' means continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The chemical name of baking soda is:
questions.why: Its formula is NaHCO3.

questions.q: Who is called the 'Father of Goan Nationalism'?
questions.why: He founded the Goa Congress Committee in 1928.

questions.q: The right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 (Article 21A) was added by the:
questions.why: The same amendment added a duty of parents under Article 51A(k).

questions.q: India shares its longest international land border with:
questions.why: The India–Bangladesh border is about 4,097 km long.

questions.q: In its October 2026 policy, the RBI changed its monetary policy stance from neutral to:
questions.why: Announced with the 25-bp repo hike after the 63rd MPC meeting. Oct 2026.

questions.q: The Bonderam festival, with its flag-and-float parade, is celebrated on which island?
questions.why: Held on the fourth Saturday of August.

questions.q: At the GITB (Great Indian Travel Bazaar) Awards 2026, Goa was recognised as the best destination for:
questions.why: Goa won 'Best MICE Destination'; its 2025 award at TTF Mumbai was for weddings. Jul 2026.

questions.q: Under the UPI 'Tap & Pay' facility launched at the Global Fintech Fest 2026, payments up to what amount need no UPI PIN?
questions.why: NFC-based tap payments at PoS terminals; higher amounts need the PIN. Sep 2026.

questions.q: The Ten Degree Channel separates:
opts: the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands
questions.why: It lies between Little Andaman and Car Nicobar.

questions.q: Operation Southern Readiness 26-2, a multinational maritime exercise hosted in India for the first time, was held at:
questions.why: It was run under Combined Task Force 154 at the Southern Naval Command. Jul 2026.

questions.q: Manoj is the brother of Rahul. Rahul is the mother of Anil. How is Manoj related to Anil?
questions.why: Draw the family tree from the statements; the answer is Maternal uncle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks an item 25% above cost and gives a 10% discount. What is the overall gain?
questions.why: Net = (1 + 25/100)(1 − 10/100) − 1 = 12.5%. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In a row of 45 students, Rahul is 16th from the left and Sita is 17th from the right. How many students sit between them?
questions.why: Between them = 45 − (16 + 17) = 12. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In a row of 42 students, Manoj is 9th from the left and Lata is 17th from the right. How many students sit between them?
questions.why: Between them = 42 − (9 + 17) = 16. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Statements: All rivers are lakes. No lakes are ponds. Conclusions: I. Some rivers are ponds. II. All rivers are ponds.
questions.why: Checked against every possible diagram of the statements: I need not be true, II need not be true. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What comes next? HIJ, LMN, PQR, TUV, …
questions.why: Each group starts 4 letters after the last one, with the same pattern inside: XYZ. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Neha walks 6 m North, then turns left and walks 7 m, then turns right and walks 9 m. Which direction is Neha facing now?
questions.why: Follow each turn from the first direction: the last leg is towards the North. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The present ages of Anil and Rekha are in the ratio 6 : 2. After 2 years the ratio will be 8 : 3. What is Rekha's present age?
questions.why: Let the ages be 6k and 2k: (6k + 2)/(2k + 2) = 8/3 gives k = 5, so Rekha is 10. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The present ages of Ravi and Rahul are in the ratio 6 : 5. After 8 years the ratio will be 38 : 33. What is Rahul's present age?
questions.why: Let the ages be 6k and 5k: (6k + 8)/(5k + 8) = 38/33 gives k = 5, so Rahul is 25. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: If SCHOOL is written as TEKSTR in a certain code, how is POTENCY written in that code?
questions.why: In the code the 1st letter moves 1 place, the 2nd 2 places, the 3rd 3 places, and so on: POTENCY → QQWISIF. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: According to §99, investigating the case is generally easier in acute than in chronic disease because:
opts: acute diseases have fewer symptoms in every case
acute diseases do not need individualisation
all the phenomena are recent and still fresh in the patient's memory
questions.why: §99: in acute disease the symptoms are recent and striking, so the investigation is easier and quicker.

questions.q: In Kent's sixth observation, too short a relief of symptoms after a remedy points to:
opts: organic (structural) changes or something interfering with the remedy
a remedy that was too deep for the case
questions.why: Kent: amelioration that lasts too short a time suggests structural change in the organs, or in acute cases a rapidly advancing process.

questions.q: In Materia Medica, a 'modality' is:
opts: the sensation felt by the patient
the pathological diagnosis of the disease
a condition that makes a symptom better or worse
questions.why: A modality is any circumstance (time, temperature, motion, position, food, weather) that ameliorates or aggravates a symptom.

questions.q: 'The Encyclopedia of Pure Materia Medica' in ten volumes was compiled by:
questions.why: Timothy Field Allen compiled the 10-volume Encyclopedia of Pure Materia Medica (1874–1879), a schematic pure Materia Medica.

questions.q: Large, knotty stools held together by threads of mucus are characteristic of:
questions.why: Graphites: constipation with large, difficult, knotty stools united by mucous threads (Allen's Keynotes).

questions.q: Graphites used in homoeopathy is:
questions.why: Graphites is plumbago or black lead; vegetable charcoal is Carbo veg., flint is Silicea and animal charcoal is Carbo animalis.

questions.q: Tablets used in homoeopathy are made of:
questions.why: Homoeopathic tablets are pressed from lactose; globules and pilules are made of cane sugar.

questions.q: Hahnemann's first index of symptoms appeared as Part 2 of:
opts: the first edition of the Organon
questions.why: The second part of the Fragmenta (1805) was an index of symptoms, the forerunner of the repertory.

questions.q: The rubric 'Mind, Fastidious' means:
opts: excessively particular about neatness and details
questions.why: Fastidious patients, such as Arsenicum, insist on order and exactness in small things.

questions.q: After about 24 hours of fasting, blood glucose is maintained mainly by:
opts: absorption of glucose from the gut
release of free glucose from muscle glycogen
questions.why: Liver glycogen is largely used up within about a day; muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase and cannot release free glucose.

questions.q: Diabetic ketoacidosis typically produces:
opts: high anion gap metabolic acidosis with deep, rapid (Kussmaul) breathing
questions.why: Ketoacids add unmeasured anions, widening the anion gap; the lungs compensate by blowing off CO₂.

questions.q: In chronic typhoid carriers the bacilli most often persist in the:
questions.why: Chronic carriers harbour Salmonella Typhi in the gall bladder (often with gallstones) and excrete it in faeces.

questions.q: The mature cyst of Entamoeba histolytica contains:
questions.why: The mature infective cyst of E. histolytica is quadrinucleate; the cyst of the non-pathogenic E. coli has up to eight nuclei.

questions.q: Bronchitis in an old person with coarse rattling of mucus but very little expectoration, drowsiness and a thick white-coated tongue calls for:
questions.why: Ant tart has loud rattling with little expectoration, drowsiness and prostration, typical in the very young and the very old.

questions.q: Eczema with thick, leathery crusts under which thick white pus collects, with intolerable itching, calls for:
questions.why: Mezereum has eruptions covered by thick, hard crusts with pus beneath, intensely itchy, especially on the scalp.

questions.q: Jaundice with an enlarged, tender liver, clay-coloured stools and a tendency to gallstones, for which the mother tincture is often used, calls for:
questions.why: Chionanthus is a liver remedy for jaundice, hepatic enlargement, clay-coloured stools and gallstone colic.

questions.q: A 'chocolate cyst' of the ovary is characteristic of:
questions.why: An endometrioma contains old altered blood that looks like chocolate.

questions.q: Under Anemia Mukt Bharat, a pregnant woman takes one IFA tablet (60 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid) daily from the second trimester for at least:
questions.why: Prophylactic IFA is given daily from the 4th month of pregnancy for a minimum of 180 days, and continued for 180 days post partum.

questions.q: A 'thumb sign' on a lateral neck X-ray of a toxic, drooling child is diagnostic of:
questions.why: The swollen epiglottis appears as a thumb; croup shows a steeple sign on an AP view.

questions.q: The basic treatment of an established abscess is:
questions.why: 'Where there is pus, let it out': pus must be drained; antibiotics alone do not penetrate an abscess cavity.

questions.q: In adults, the paranasal sinus most commonly involved in sinusitis is the:
questions.why: The maxillary sinus is most often affected in adults; the ethmoids are most often affected in children.

questions.q: Retention of flatus with distension after abdominal operations, with no passage of gas up or down, calls for:
questions.why: Raphanus is the noted remedy for postoperative gas retention.

questions.q: A firearm entry wound is characterised by:
opts: everted margins without an abrasion collar
a wound larger than the exit wound in all cases
inverted margins with an abrasion collar
questions.why: Entry wounds are small with inverted edges and an abrasion (contusion) collar; exit wounds are usually larger and everted, without a collar.

questions.q: Horrock's apparatus is used to find:
opts: the dose of bleaching powder needed to disinfect well water
questions.why: Horrock's apparatus estimates the amount of bleaching powder needed to give a free residual chlorine in water.

questions.q: The denominator of the perinatal mortality rate is:
opts: live births plus still births in the year
questions.why: Perinatal mortality rate = (still births of 28 weeks or more + deaths in the first 7 days) per 1,000 live births plus still births.
